title: Es importante que practiques
blurbEn: A list of advice on the fridge door, and the pattern behind every line of it: es + adjective + que.
body:
Mi profesora me ha dado una lista de consejos para el examen.

Es importante que practiques todos los días, aunque sea diez minutos.

Es mejor que leas textos completos que listas de palabras sueltas.

Es normal que te equivoques. Es raro que alguien no se equivoque.

No es necesario que entiendas todo. Es suficiente con que entiendas lo esencial.

Es una pena que la gente abandone justo cuando empieza a mejorar.

Y la última, subrayada dos veces: es fundamental que hables, aunque te dé vergüenza.

He puesto la lista en la nevera, al lado de la foto de mis abuelos.

Ojalá le haga caso.
translationEn:
My teacher has given me a list of tips for the exam.

It's important that you practise every day, even if it's only ten minutes.

It's better to read whole texts than lists of isolated words.

It's normal to get things wrong. It's strange for anyone not to get things wrong.

It isn't necessary to understand everything. It's enough to understand the essentials.

It's a shame that people give up just when they start to improve.

And the last one, underlined twice: it's essential that you speak, even if it embarrasses you.

I've put the list on the fridge, next to the photo of my grandparents.

I hope I take my own advice.

practiques.note: 'Es importante que' + subjunctive. Every 'es + adjective + que' works this way.

dé.note: Subjunctive of 'dar', with an accent so it is not read as the preposition 'de'.

haga caso.note: 'hacer caso' is to pay attention. 'Ojalá le haga caso' — I hope I listen to it.

phrases.gloss: It's normal to get things wrong
